rules.statement: an adapter turns a generated sink into another tool shape, and judges nothing
rules.remedy: it only translates; a rule about what is allowed belongs in the manifest

rules.statement: the CLI parses arguments, calls the facade and picks a reporter — nothing else
rules.remedy: add the capability to ArchCheck instead: the agent hook does not shell out

rules.statement: a contract kind decides, emits and explains — it never runs anything
rules.remedy: return the decision as data and let a probe do the walking — a walk belongs in src/graph/syntax.ts, and the contract reads the fact it produced

rules.statement: coverage counts rules and renders a table, and checks nothing
rules.remedy: take the rules and the counts as arguments; do not go looking for them

rules.statement: the emitter asks a contract kind for fragments and never runs a probe
rules.remedy: emit is a pure function of the manifest; move the runtime part to a probe

rules.statement: every error-severity rule has a fixture it is proven to catch
rules.remedy: add fixtures/rules/<id>.violation.ts that deliberately breaks this rule — a rule matching nothing passes every build and looks exactly like compliance

rules.statement: exceptions decide suppression from paths and dates, and run no check
rules.remedy: take the diagnostics as an argument rather than producing them

rules.statement: a filename is camelCase, or kebab-case when it names a contract kind
rules.remedy: rename the file

rules.statement: fixture verification places a fixture and runs the checks, and declares no rule
rules.remedy: it proves a rule catches something; the rule itself belongs in the manifest

rules.statement: the graph reader reports facts and evaluates no rule
rules.remedy: move the judgement into a contract kind; the graph only observes

rules.statement: init reads the folder structure and the graph, and runs no rule
rules.remedy: infer it from what the code already does; do not evaluate a rule here

rules.statement: the kernel imports nothing internal — not a layer, and not the TypeScript SDK
rules.remedy: if the kernel needs it, it is not the kernel: move the type down or the code up

rules.statement: a dynamic import names its module literally, so the graph stays complete
rules.remedy: import the candidates statically and pick between them

rules.statement: logging goes through one seam, so the server stays embeddable
rules.remedy: return the text and let the CLI print it

rules.statement: a caught error is handled, rethrown, or its silence is explained
rules.remedy: handle it, rethrow it, or leave a comment saying why ignoring is safe

rules.statement: an exception lives in the manifest with an owner and an expiry, never inline
rules.remedy: declare an exception in architecture.config.ts, with an owner and an expiry

rules.statement: the normaliser enriches a finding and runs no check of its own
rules.remedy: inject it, the way refine is injected, rather than importing a kind

rules.statement: the facade is the one place the layers are wired together
rules.remedy: wire it in src/archcheck.ts — that is the composition root, and the only one

rules.statement: a probe returns evidence, never prose and never a verdict
rules.remedy: return a RawFinding and let the kind's explain() write the sentence

rules.statement: the registry knows that a rule has a kind, never what a kind means
rules.remedy: inject the kind-specific behaviour as a parameter, the way validateParams is

rules.statement: a reporter reads a RunResult and reaches for nothing else
rules.remedy: put what the reporter needs into the Diagnostic, so every audience gets it

rules.statement: a test may reach any layer, because its job is to look at one
rules.remedy: nothing to do — tests are exempt from the layer law by design

rules.statement: the baseline reads and writes one file and knows nothing about rules
rules.remedy: take the diagnostics as an argument; the baseline only keys off identity

rules.statement: the filesystem seam reads and writes and decides nothing
rules.remedy: return the paths and let a probe judge them

rules.statement: the manifest imports archcheck through its public surface, like any consumer
rules.remedy: import from './src/index.js' — reaching inside would make the manifest a consumer no other repo could be

rules.statement: a utility reaches the kernel and nothing else
rules.remedy: take what you need as an argument instead of importing it
